title: June Folds Its Beach Towel
skyStory: The last night of June brings a seventeen percent moon in Taurus, curled up like a cat on a windowsill after a long, warm day. June is packing up. It folds its beach towel, shakes the sand from its sandals and leaves a note for July: be nice to them. The moon reads the note and tucks it under a cloud for safekeeping.

reading: June is ending, and the cabin is quiet in that satisfied, end-of-a-good-month way. Remember the seven-word goal from June 1? Tonight is the report. Be honest. Be generous with yourself. Half done is still half the mountain climbed.

Look back at the month: the doodle, the goats, the orange cat, the longest day. You started a lot. You finished more than you think. The [[Ten of Pentacles]] is quietly counting the treasures you built this month without even noticing. Accept the count. Then fold your own towel and get ready for July.
joel.mission: Write your seven-word June report, send it to Nancy, then write one seven-word wish for July.
joel.omen: A sunset that lingers longer than expected. The month is saying goodbye slowly because it liked you.

reading: The shore is quiet tonight, the tide low, the sand still warm from the day. June has been good to you. You crossed a little further, rested a little deeper, celebrated a solstice and a half-birthday. Not bad for thirty days.

Send Joel your seven-word report, then let the month go. Do not analyse it. Do not plan July yet. Just stand at the edge of the water and say thank you to June, out loud, even if only the gulls hear. They will tell everyone on the beach by morning.
nancy.mission: Say thank you to June out loud, outside, and list three favourite moments from the month.
nancy.omen: A gull flying away over the water. The month is leaving, but it is taking good memories with it.

together.text: June report. Each of you send your seven-word summary of the month, exactly seven words again, to match June 1. Read the other's twice. Then each name one moment from June you want to remember forever. Fold it up and save it.

game.intro: June is folding its beach towel and heading home. Show us a little summer before it goes.
game.prompt: Something striped: towel, umbrella, shirt, awning. Zoom in until the stripes look like a highway.
